title: Live server never initializes the books table — schema created on a discarded connection
evidence: src/main.rs:79 binds `db` to a fresh rusqlite::Connection::open_in_memory() whose schema is never created; src/main.rs:80 runs TABLE_DEF via models::create_connection("in-memory") on a SEPARATE file-backed connection (SQLite open() treats "in-memory" as a path, not :memory:) and discards it with .ok(); src/main.rs:82 wraps the schema-less `db` into app state. The 12288-byte on-disk `in-memory` SQLite artifact (verified: contains a `books` table) is that discarded connection's output. At runtime every /books route (list/create/get/update/delete in src/database.rs) errors with `no such table: books`.
suggestion: Run conn.execute_batch(models::TABLE_DEF) on `db` itself before wrapping it (or bind db_data to the connection returned by create_connection); using a persistent file path would also satisfy the 'not just in-memory state' clause of R7.

title: Passing tests mask the runtime schema bug — every test builds its own initialized connection
evidence: src/main.rs:107-111 create_db() and src/database.rs:144-148 get_test_conn() both run conn.execute_batch(TABLE_DEF) on a locally-built connection, so the 21 tests never exercise the broken main() wiring. test_coverage=1.0 in scores.json reflects this masked state.
suggestion: Add an integration test that boots the actual main() server wiring (or a shared init function) so the schema-init path is covered.
